NEXATIK EXPLAINED

Your questions,
answered.

Is NexaTik free to use?+

The current 0.5.2 release is free to download and use. A paid activation system or ten-video trial limit is not included in this release.

Which platforms can I select?+

The app includes YouTube, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok link inputs. Availability depends on the selected platform, the content and any login or verification requirements. A thumbnail or a loaded list does not mean a video has finished downloading.

Can I download more than one video?+

Yes. Paste multiple video links or load an available profile list, select the videos you want, then choose Download selected. The editable profile scan limit controls how many matching items to load.

What goes into the ZIP file?+

When automatic ZIP is enabled, the batch archive contains successfully completed videos and their matching title/description text files, including valid selected files skipped because they already exist. Failed and partial files are excluded.

How do dates and scheduled downloads work?+

Upload dates filter the original video publication date. A scheduled batch starts at your selected future time while NexaTik remains open and the laptop stays awake and connected to the internet. Closing the app cancels its pending schedule.

Why does Instagram open a browser?+

In version 0.5.2, Instagram profile links use a visible Chrome Reels scan, with Edge as a launch fallback. Complete any requested login or verification in that browser. The scan waits up to three minutes and collects visible Reels; complete profile coverage is not guaranteed.

How do I get an update?+

Version 0.5.0 and later include an Updates button. When a newer stable release is published, the app can offer Install update. Earlier installations need a one-time full setup installation. Updates wait for active or scheduled work before installation.

Can I save any video I find?+

Only download content you own or have permission to save, and only where the platform permits it. This app does not grant rights to third-party content or access to private accounts.
